dataset.title: Oil net import dependence, % of supply (EI via OWID, derived)

indicator.name: Oil net import dependence
indicator.description: 100 × (oil total energy supply − oil production) ÷ supply, same country and year, both in TWh from the Energy Institute Statistical Review (via Our World in Data). Positive = share of supply that has to be imported net; negative = net exporter.

source.name: Our World in Data – Energy dataset (Energy Institute Statistical Review data)
source.license: Our World in Data processing: CC BY 4.0. Underlying data: Energy Institute Statistical Review, free to use with citation (see upstream).

upstream.license: Free to access, citation required ("Energy Institute – Statistical Review of World Energy (2026)"); no open licence is stated on the EI pages checked on 2026-10-12

notes: Computed by npm run data:import: for each entity, the latest year in which both supply and production have a number and supply is above 0. Entities with no such year are kept as missing.
EI covers about 80 countries individually; smaller countries are only in EI regional totals, so they have no value here.
caveats: Net of exports and ignores stock changes: a country that imports and re-exports shows only the net. It is an economy-wide average, not specific to power plants.
Oil supply (all products) and production (crude, condensates, NGLs) are not exactly the same product scope; treat values near 0 as rough.

scoring.rationale: A real net-import share for one fuel, used inside the electricity import exposure. Not scored separately: on its own it ignores how much of the energy system the fuel serves.
